prediction.likelyOutcome: Navient should recover its conceded $503,822.72 cooling tower claim in full, reduced by a setoff on BPG's counterclaim that is more likely than not to land well below BPG's $817,845 ask -- probably in the $150,000-$300,000 range once the heat pump age-based theory is discounted, the rooftop units are priced at or near BPG's own expert's $8,400 repair figure, and the transformer claim is barred or substantially reduced on limitations grounds. Net to Navient, the likeliest range is a positive recovery in the low-to-mid hundreds of thousands of dollars, with prevailing-party fees also probably favoring Navient though unquantified on this record.

issues.label: Transformer Counterclaim / Statute of Limitations Defense

outcome.description: The Superior Court entered post-trial judgment for Navient in $503,822.72 (the conceded cooling-tower reimbursement) less $79,650 awarded to BPG on its counterclaim ($71,250 to repair 25 non-operational heat pumps and $8,400 to repair two rooftop air units), a net principal of $424,172.72 plus prejudgment interest from March 17, 2020; BPG's transformer and elevator claims failed. Navient was held the prevailing party entitled to its attorneys' fees and expenses under lease section 28(q) (amount not stated). This is the trial-level decision; no appeal is reflected in the source.
